outcome: One consolidated all-flash platform that gives clinical systems more predictable performance while freeing up rack space.
overview: Hospital storage grows in the shape of its procurements: an array bought for imaging, another for the clinical record, a third for everything else, each with its own support date and its own performance characteristics. PowerStore consolidates that onto one all-flash platform with inline data reduction. The clinically important property is predictable latency for the systems clinicians wait on, and the honest way to size for it is measured performance data rather than a data-reduction ratio quoted from a datasheet.

benefits.text: Separate arrays with separate support dates consolidate onto one platform
benefits.limits: Sized from measured capacity and performance data; a design built on invoice history or on projected growth alone produces a quotation rather than an architecture

benefits.text: All-flash media gives predictable latency for the clinical systems staff wait on
benefits.limits: Predictability depends on the array not being run to its limits; a design sized to headline capacity rather than measured performance loses exactly this property

benefits.text: Inline data reduction reduces the raw capacity purchased for the same usable data
benefits.limits: Reduction ratios are entirely data-dependent; imaging data typically reduces far less than general file data, and quoting a general ratio to a hospital is misleading

residency: Clinical data remains on customer-owned arrays inside the hospital data centre

notFor.situation: An estate with current arrays under support and adequate measured performance
notFor.why: Consolidation without a support or performance driver is change for its own sake
Scale-out file and object platforms fit that profile better than primary block storage

scope:
Model: Redington solutions engineering with an accredited Dell implementation partner · Duration: 8–12 weeks to a migrated estate, hardware lead time excluded
Support model: Vendor hardware support with a replacement term matched to clinical criticality; Redington coordinates the vendor case.
1) Assessment — capacity, measured performance, data-reduction sample and downtime tolerances
2) Design — sizing at the measured ratio, migration order and rollback plan
3) Deploy — array installed, presented and validated
4) Migrate and hand over — workloads migrated within their tolerances, operations handed over
deliverables: Achieved reduction on migrated data is within the range the design assumed
Every clinical migration completes within its agreed downtime tolerance or is rolled back inside it
Measured latency for the clinical systems in scope meets the design figure
effort: 8–12 weeks to a migrated estate, hardware lead time excluded
